correctness.rationale: For every SPD 2 by 2 A with exactly two iid standard Gaussian probes, polar decomposition gives a rank-one Nyström residual with scalar tau. Conditional centered Gaussian quadratic forms give variance 2 E[tau^2]; Fourier expansion of tau and radial integration give cross-covariance (ab/2)(1+r^4). Therefore true trace-estimator variance and expected posterior error square are X+Y and X-Y. Explicit positive polynomial factorizations prove sharp 5/8 and 5/3 bounds including unique equality at equal eigenvalues; finite code checks verify the nonstandard algebra and moments without being substituted for proof.

The predecessor Nyström++ uses a fixed split. Database claim searches did not surface equivalent exact formulas. value.rationale: Posterior squared error is a native numerical estimator output used for accuracy decisions and adaptive stopping; it is systematically optimistic due to the correlated leave-one-out corrections. The exact all-spectra planar formula, largest possible 5/3 underreporting factor and sharp fixed-budget Gaussian comparator quantify a natural small-query regime not covered by the source explicit large-sample spectral theorem. This is a complete, motivated endpoint classification, not an arbitrary slice. It is limited to baseline unnormalized methods, and is not a practical superiority claim because full-rank reconstruction and the normalized variant can be exact at this dimension.
